title: The Milky Way and Nova Centauri 2013
caption: The Milky Way and Nova Centauri 2013, La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The southern Milky Way crosses this view of the night sky above ESO's La Silla Observatory, a sea of stars from edge to edge. On the left stands the Swedish-ESO Submillimeter Telescope, known as SEST.

Among all those stars, one is special and shining brightly. It is Nova Centauri 2013, also known as V1369 Centauri. A nova is a star system that suddenly flares up far brighter than normal, then gradually fades back over time. When that happens, a star that was once hard to see can briefly stand out in the sky.
The telescopes at La Silla are built to watch the heavens, and on this night the camera caught the southern Milky Way with a newly brightened star among its crowd.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph at ESO's La Silla Observatory, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A camera exposure can gather far more light than the eye, so the Milky Way may look richer and brighter than it would to someone standing there.
